run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The hotel-reservation application's user-facing hotel search path is broken. The frontend's HTTP GET /hotels returns 500 on every request in the sampled traces, and each failing /hotels span has a single child client span /search.Search/Nearby with error=true / otel.status_code=ERROR that fails in 13-44 microseconds, while /recommendations, profile and recommendation calls in the same sample complete with 200/no errors. The search backend has no pod and no Service endpoints: the last search pod (search-567bb6c4b8-cj9jx) was stopped at 2026-11-24T01:52:15Z, and from 01:52:16Z its ReplicaSet search-567bb6c4b8 was repeatedly refused pod creation with 'is forbidden: failed quota: memory-limit-quota: must specify memory for: hotel-reserv-search'. The object that introduced that constraint is the ResourceQuota memory-limit-quota in namespace hotel-reservation, created 2026-11-24T01:52:15Z (field manager OpenAPI-Generator), hard memory 1Gi, while the hotel-reserv-search container declares only cpu resources (limits cpu 1000m, requests cpu 100m) and so is rejected by quota admission. The Deployment search therefore reports 0 ready/available replicas with Available=False (MinimumReplicasUnavailable) and ReplicaFailure=True. Conclusion: a newly applied memory ResourceQuota makes the search workload unschedulable, search is unavailable, and frontend /hotels fails; other traced dependencies (profile, recommendation) are healthy in the same sample. The actor/object that stopped the running search pod at 01:52:15Z is not recorded in the available evidence, so the exact trigger of the pod's termination remains a gap; the quota is what prevents the workload from recovering. Note also that no application container in this namespace declares a memory request, so the same quota blocks pod creation for any workload that needs a new pod.

claims.text: A ResourceQuota named memory-limit-quota exists in namespace hotel-reservation with spec.hard memory=1Gi, status.used.memory="0", metadata.creationTimestamp 2026-11-24T01:52:15Z, and managedFieldsSummary showing manager OpenAPI-Generator (Update) at 2026-11-24T01:52:15Z.

Deployment search in hotel-reservation has spec.replicas=1 but no readyReplicas and no availableReplicas, with conditions Available=False (reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable) and ReplicaFailure=True whose message is: pods "search-567bb6c4b8-npt5d" is forbidden: failed quota: memory-limit-quota: must specify memory for: hotel-reserv-search.

ReplicaSet search-567bb6c4b8 (owner Deployment search, pod-template-hash 567bb6c4b8, status.replicas 0) produced 9 FailedCreate events at 2026-11-24T01:52:16-17Z, each reading 'Error creating: pods "search-567bb6c4b8-..." is forbidden: failed quota: memory-limit-quota: must specify memory for: hotel-reserv-search', and Deployment search scaled that ReplicaSet from 0 to 1 at 2026-11-24T01:52:16Z.

The hotel-reserv-search container of Deployment search declares resources limits.cpu=1000m and requests.cpu=100m only (no memory request or limit); the Deployment has generation 1 and was last written at 2026-11-24T01:52:01Z by kubectl-client-side-apply, with kube-controller-manager updating only its status at 2026-11-24T01:52:16Z.

Pod search-567bb6c4b8-cj9jx was scheduled and its container hotel-reserv-search started at 2026-11-24T01:52:04Z, and an event 'Stopping container hotel-reserv-search' (reason Killing) for that pod is recorded at 2026-11-24T01:52:15Z; the current pod listing of the namespace (18 pods) contains no search pod at all.

Service search in hotel-reservation exposes ports 8082 (name 8082) and 9092 (name metrics) with selector io.kompose.service=search, and the corresponding Endpoints object 'search' has subsets null, i.e. no backing addresses.

At 2026-11-24T01:52:27Z, up=0 for instance search.hotel-reservation:9092 in job hotel-reservation-application, while other application/blackbox targets of the namespace listed in the same result (e.g. rate.hotel-reservation:9091, frontend.hotel-reservation:5000) report up=1.

In frontend traces for the window (last backend sample ending 2026-11-24T01:52:26.986Z), all 12 shown HTTP GET /hotels spans carry error=true with http.status_code=500 and otel.status_code=ERROR, each paired with a child client span /search.Search/Nearby that carries error=true and otel.status_code=ERROR and lasts 13-44 microseconds; trace 24aa2f5abb3909bf contains exactly these two spans (GET /hotels 500, 143us, and its child /search.Search/Nearby error, 44us).

In the same frontend trace sample, HTTP GET /recommendations spans return http.status_code=200 (8 spans, 0 error rows), and downstream profile.Profile/GetProfiles (8 spans) and recommendation.Recommendation/GetRecommendations (8 spans) have 0 error rows, with profile child spans mongo_profile and memcached_get_profile also showing 0 errors.
Jaeger's service list for this target contains frontend, profile, recommendation, reservation and user only; no search service appears among them.

rate_requests_received_total for rate.hotel-reservation:9091 (job hotel-reservation-application) equals 0 at 2026-11-24T01:52:27Z, and probe_success for rate.hotel-reservation:8084 equals 1 at that same instant.

Blackbox probe_success values at 2026-11-24T01:52:27Z include 0 for the ingress probe instance http://ingress-nginx-controller.ingress-nginx/api/hotels?inDate=2015-04-09&outDate=2015-04-10&lat=38.0235&lon=-122.095 and 0 for search.hotel-reservation:8082, but also 0 for frontend.hotel-reservation:5000, geo.hotel-reservation:8083, profile.hotel-reservation:8081 and user.hotel-reservation:8086; 1 for rate:8084, recommendation:8085 and reservation:8087. The earliest points of that series are 01:50:27Z and 01:51:07Z, which precede the pods' starts (01:52:02-01:52:13Z).

Pod geo-d4c78b89b-blnl5 (container hotel-reserv-geo) recorded normal startup between 01:52:02Z and 01:52:12Z, connected to mongodb-geo:27017, and logged 'Successfully registered in consul' for srv-geo with no error/failure lines in the 20 returned lines.

Pod user-5ccf6db68f-ddnfb (container hotel-reserv-user) started at 01:52:05Z, connected to mongodb-user:27017, generated test data and logged 'Successfully registered in consul' for srv-user at 01:52:13Z, with no error lines in the 20 returned lines.

Pod frontend-68745cb99c-8lgbw logged successful startup at 01:52:02Z, initializing gRPC clients including srv-search, srv-profile, srv-recommendation, srv-user and srv-reservation, then 'Serving http'; the 31 returned lines contain no error lines and no request-handling lines.

The ConfigMaps present in hotel-reservation are failure-admin-geo (keys remove-admin-mongo.sh, remove-mitigate-admin-geo-mongo.sh, revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh, revoke-mitigate-admin-geo-mongo.sh), failure-admin-rate (analogous rate/mongo scripts), kube-root-ca.crt, mongo-geo-script and mongo-rate-script; none references search or the memory quota.

The breaking setting is the memory requirement injected by ResourceQuota memory-limit-quota (hard memory 1Gi) into a namespace whose application containers declare no memory request: the quota's admission check is what names hotel-reserv-search in every pod-creation rejection, so search cannot be rescheduled while the quota stands.

The missing memory request on every hotel-reservation application container (for example Deployment search's hotel-reserv-search: only limits.cpu=1000m and requests.cpu=100m) is the configuration weakness the new quota binds on; even after the immediate search outage is fixed, any pod rescheduled in this namespace would be rejected the same way unless memory requests are added or the quota is removed.

The /hotels failures are not explained by a general frontend problem or by profile/recommendation failure: in the same frontend trace sample, /recommendations returned 200 and profile/recommendation/memcached/mongo child spans show no errors, while every failing /hotels span failed on its /search.Search/Nearby child.

Latency, queueing or overload in the rate service does not explain the /hotels 500s: the failing /search.Search/Nearby spans end in 13-44 microseconds with an error status rather than timing out against the retry settings (RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS=1000, RATE_RPC_MAX_ATTEMPTS=2), search has no endpoint at all, and rate_requests_received_total was 0 at 01:52:27Z while rate's own probe_success was 1.

Add memory requests (and matching limits) to the hotel-reserv-search container - and to the other application containers that declare only cpu - or adjust/remove ResourceQuota memory-limit-quota, then confirm a search pod is created and that frontend HTTP GET /hotels returns 200 with /search.Search/Nearby spans succeeding.

gaps: No evidence records who or what stopped pod search-567bb6c4b8-cj9jx at 2026-11-24T01:52:15Z: there is no ReplicaSet SuccessfulDelete event for it and no Eviction event, and the pod no longer exists, so its last termination reason, exit code and container logs could not be read (fetch of a deleted pod is unavailable).

The stop of the search pod and the creation of ResourceQuota memory-limit-quota share the timestamp 2026-11-24T01:52:15Z, but no change-history source is configured (change_history is not integrated), so the applying actor behind manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' and the ordering of the two actions could not be verified.

ReplicaSet search-567bb6c4b8 carries creationTimestamp 2026-11-24T01:52:16Z although it recorded 'Created pod: search-567bb6c4b8-cj9jx' at 01:52:04Z; whether that ReplicaSet was deleted and recreated could not be determined from the available evidence.

The blackbox probe signal is ambiguous: probe_success is 0 at 01:52:27Z for frontend:5000, geo:8083, profile:8081, user:8086 and search:8082, yet frontend and profile demonstrably served successful requests in traces, so those probe readings cannot be used on their own as health or impact evidence; the earliest probe points (01:50:27Z, 01:51:07Z) precede pod startup and give no pre-fault baseline.

Prometheus holds no traces_span_metrics_* series for this target: queries for traces_span_metrics_calls_total (name and label based) returned no data, so span-based error rates and a before/after comparison could not be computed; the collected metric samples for the namespace start around 01:50:27Z (metric series) and the last probe point is 01:52:27Z, so no pre-incident latency baseline exists and no latency trend is claimed.

Error-tagged trace queries for services reservation and user returned no matching traces (no_data), which is not proof that those services had no errors; their health is unverified beyond startup log lines.

Traces come from a biased backend sample (traces_search returned exactly the requested 20 traces and reports incomplete, more may exist); counts of failing /hotels spans describe only the returned sample, not the request rate.
Kubernetes reads are point-in-time observations at approximately 01:52:29-01:54:39Z, after the incident window ended at 01:52:27Z; the object states above are not a historical record of the window.
next_steps: Add memory requests/limits to the hotel-reserv-search container (or delete/adjust ResourceQuota memory-limit-quota) and confirm Deployment search reaches 1 ready replica and Service search gains endpoints.

Audit the other hotel-reservation application containers (frontend, geo, profile, rate, recommendation, reservation, user) which declare only cpu resources, since the current quota would reject their pod creation on any reschedule.

Check with the platform/change owner which tool applied ResourceQuota memory-limit-quota at 2026-11-24T01:52:15Z (field manager OpenAPI-Generator) and what deleted the search pod at the same time, since change history is not available to this investigation.
Re-run the /hotels path after recovery to confirm 200 responses and successful /search.Search/Nearby server spans from the search service in Jaeger.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

notes: Lists what this Jaeger has seen since it last started, with no time range: a name missing here does not prove it does not exist, and a Jaeger restart empties the list.
